z-m-04-01.title: Wetin next card fit come out?
z-m-04-01.topic: Possibility: saying wetin fit come and wetin no fit come
z-m-04-01.goal: Each time dem draw card, update and state 'fit come / no fit come / must come' with reason.
z-m-04-01.material: Box get 6 number cards, each with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6. Back of all cards same, so you draw one by one with eyes closed. After you check drawn card front, put am aside and no return am to box. Notices below go open one by one.
z-m-04-01.thinking.2: Doubting reasons wey sound possible, like size or order
z-m-04-01.prereq.0: Knowing numbers 1 to 10 and odd/even (Grade 1 level)
z-m-04-01.prereq.1: Separating 'there is' from 'there is not' in a statement
z-m-04-01.s.s1.prompt: Notices go show one by one. Each time, choose correct statement.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.hint.0: For each notice, first write 'which cards dey left in box now.'
z-m-04-01.s.s1.hint.1: For every card left, work out whether e fit come; check whether your statement correct.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.info: Nobody draw card yet. Think about first card you go draw.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.after: Any card wey dey box fit come, and card wey no dey box like 7 no fit come. You no fit know beforehand which one go come.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You see say 5 dey box, so e fit come. First look at cards wey dey there na good idea.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Only cards 1 to 6 dey box. Check again whether card wey no dey box fit come.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.r.c: If you draw with eyes closed, you no fit know in advance which card e go be. 'Fit come' and 'must come' no be same.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Card wey come go be one of 1 to 6
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You check all cards for box and state range of possible results. You no choose one number.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.info: You draw two cards and get 5 and 2. Put both aside, no return dem. Now think about third card.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.after: 5 and 2 don leave box and no go return. So 5 no fit come again; remaining cards 1, 3, 4, 6 fit all come. New information change one of your first ideas.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You think situation still like at beginning. Check where 5 dey now.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 5 and 2 don come, so na 1 turn now
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.r.b: No fixed turn. If you draw with eyes closed, any remaining card fit come.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.o.c: One of remaining cards 1, 3, 4, 6 go come
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You look only at cards left inside box and forget cards put aside. You use new information for judgment.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.o.d: 5 and 2 don come, so this time 6 must come
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Some cards don come already, but next one no decided. Look how many cards remain.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.info: 4 come as third card. You put 4 aside too. Now three cards, 1, 3, 6, remain inside box.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.ask: Choose correct statement about fourth card you go draw.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.after: Among remaining cards 1, 3, 6, odd ones (1, 3) and even one (6) dey. So both types fit come. Even though cards fewer, you still no fit know beforehand which card go come.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Check one by one whether any even number remain.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.o.b: 6 na biggest number, so 6 most likely to come
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Bigger number no easier to draw. All card backs same and you draw with eyes closed.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You put 4 aside. Check whether 4 dey box now.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Both odd card and even card fit come
z-m-04-01.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You notice say among remaining 1, 3, 6, odd and even numbers both dey.
z-m-04-01.s.s1.reflect: How your idea say 5 fit come change after dem put 5 aside? Which statement stay same even after dem draw more cards?
z-m-04-01.s.s2.prompt: Friend talk, 'Cards left na 1, 3, 6, so biggest, 6, go come!' Wetin you wan tell friend?
z-m-04-01.s.s2.hint.0: Think whether you fit change your friend words 'go come' to 'fit come.'
z-m-04-01.s.s2.hint.1: Work out whether e really impossible for any card apart from 6 to come among three cards left.
z-m-04-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Difference between 'fit come' and 'must come' show in wetin I say?
z-m-04-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You think say other cards among remaining 1, 3, 6 fit come too?
z-m-04-01.s.s2.model.0: 6 fit come, but e no must. 1 or 3 fit come.
z-m-04-01.s.s2.modelNote.0: You considered all cards wey fit come.
z-m-04-01.s.s2.model.1: Bigger number no easier to draw. You draw with eyes closed, so you no fit know which card go come.
z-m-04-01.s.s2.model.2: 6 fit come, but no be must. 1 or 3 fit come too.

z-m-04-03.title: One stain cover one box
z-m-04-03.topic: Data wey hide inside table: wetin else we need to find am?
z-m-04-03.goal: Choose the information wey you need to find one box for table (the total number, whether each person choose only one thing), then talk how the answer go change wen new information come.
z-m-04-03.material: Each friend for our class choose one kind vehicle wey dem like. Paint cover one box for the survey table, so nobody fit see am. [Table] Car 6 / Train □ (nobody fit see) / Airplane 4 / Ship 2. You wan know the number wey go enter empty box (□).
z-m-04-03.thinking.2: Correct your judgment wen new information come
z-m-04-03.prereq.0: Add and subtract numbers up to 20 (Grade 1 level)
z-m-04-03.prereq.1: Read number of people for each box in table
z-m-04-03.s.s1.prompt: Wetin else you need know to find number wey go enter □? Choose all correct answers.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.hint.0: First check all the known numbers inside the boxes for table.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.hint.1: Think how that number must connect to the whole class.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.o.a: Which group the 4 people wey choose airplane dey
z-m-04-03.s.s1.r.a: Who dey which group no get anything to do with the number for □. Look again at the information wey you need to decide the number.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.o.b: Whether the friends wey choose train tall pass others
z-m-04-03.s.s1.r.b: Height no get anything to do with number for □. Think what information go let you decide the number.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.o.c: How many friends dey for the whole class
z-m-04-03.s.s1.r.c: You try make the table total match the known boxes.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.o.d: Whether the numbers for the three known boxes (car, airplane, ship) correct
z-m-04-03.s.s1.r.d: The known numbers dey already inside the table. To decide □, you need information wey no dey inside the table.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.o.e: Whether each person choose only one thing
z-m-04-03.s.s1.r.e: You try check say nobody dey appear inside two boxes.
z-m-04-03.s.s1.explain: If you know the total number of people for class and say each person choose only one thing, the number wey remain after you subtract the three known boxes na □. Knowing the height or name of friend wey choose train, or just checking the known boxes again, no fit decide □.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.prompt: Teacher tell you: '15 of us dey for our class. One friend no come today, so we no fit survey that person. Every friend wey we survey choose only one thing.' How many be □?
z-m-04-03.s.s2.hint.0: The friend wey no come no dey anywhere for table. First decide how many people suppose dey inside the table.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.hint.1: Compare that number with the numbers for the three known boxes.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.r.a: E look like you use all 15 people for class as e be. Check the information say one friend no do the survey.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.r.b: Now you know the total number of people and say each choose only one thing. Check again whether that information let you decide □.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.r.c: You compare the known boxes with the number of people wey do the survey. You use the information say one friend no come.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.r.d: Check wetin you leave out wen you count the numbers for known boxes.
z-m-04-03.s.s2.explain: The friends wey do survey na 14, that is 15 minus the 1 wey no come. The known boxes na 6 + 4 + 2 = 12, so □ na 14 − 12 = 2.
z-m-04-03.s.s3.prompt: If one more friend no come, how many friends for choose train? Write how you know.
z-m-04-03.s.s3.hint.0: Read again the total number wey you just use find □.
z-m-04-03.s.s3.hint.1: First talk wetin go happen to that total if one more friend no come.
z-m-04-03.s.s3.placeholder: Example: If more friends no come, ...
z-m-04-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: The numbers wey I write use both the numbers in the three known boxes and the number of people wey do survey?
z-m-04-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain why only □ change, and no be the other boxes, if one more friend no come?
z-m-04-03.s.s3.model.0: 1. Number of friends wey do survey go reduce by one to 13. So after you put the known 6, 4 and 2 together, wetin remain na 1.
z-m-04-03.s.s3.modelNote.0: Explain using 13 minus the total of 12 wey dey inside all known boxes, the number wey remain
z-m-04-03.s.s3.model.1: One. The total reduce by one but the other boxes stay the same, so train box reduce by one.
z-m-04-03.s.s3.modelNote.1: Explain based on the change for the total
z-m-04-03.s.s3.model.2: 1 person. Number of people wey do survey become 13, and known boxes total 12, so 13-12=1.

z-m-04-02.title: When I count, the two friends' numbers different
z-m-04-02.topic: Count without missing any: find where the counting mistake happen
z-m-04-02.goal: Wen two people count different numbers, use the number for each row as evidence, learn say both fit be wrong, then find the mistake and talk one counting method wey go prevent the same mistake.
z-m-04-02.material: For desk, identical star stickers dey in three rows. Top row get 5, middle get 6 and bottom get 5. Jihu and Nari count all the stickers. Jihu talk say na 15, Nari talk say na 17. You wan find which of the two friends correct.
z-m-04-02.thinking.0: Check with evidence (the number for each row) wen results different
z-m-04-02.thinking.1: Find the wrong row for the counting
z-m-04-02.thinking.2: Think of ways to prevent missing and counting something two times
z-m-04-02.prereq.0: Count numbers in order up to 20 (Grade 1 level)
z-m-04-02.prereq.1: Count each row separately and write am down
z-m-04-02.s.s1.prompt: Look at the numbers wey the two friends count, then choose the correct statement.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.hint.0: First write how many dey for each row.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether the total from counting all three rows dey the same as the numbers wey the two friends count.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.r.a: Smaller number no mean say e correct. Check wetin happen wen you put the numbers for each row together.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.r.b: You check both numbers using the number for each row.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.r.c: You think say the person wey count more no miss any. But person fit count the same sticker two times too.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.o.d: We no fit tell who correct
z-m-04-02.s.s1.r.d: We already know the number for each row. Look again whether you fit use am check.
z-m-04-02.s.s1.explain: If you count 5 for top row, 6 for middle row and 5 for bottom row, total na 16. Jihu's 15 and Nari's 17 both no correct. Both friends make mistake somewhere while dem dey count.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.prompt: This na how Jihu count aloud. Choose the row wey wrong.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.hint.0: Count how many dem count for each row, then compare am with the known number.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.hint.1: For the words wey dem use count the bottom row, point with finger and check how many dem count.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.line.0: E count top row from left: one, two, three, four, five.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.line.1: E count middle row from left and continue: six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.line.2: E count bottom row from left and continue: twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.line.3: The last number wey e count na fifteen, so total na 15.
z-m-04-02.s.s2.explain: Row 3 wrong. Bottom row get 5 stickers, but e count only 4: twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. E miss sixteen. E count rows 1 and 2 to match the number for each row, and row 4 just repeat the last number e count before, so the counting method itself no be the mistake.
z-m-04-02.s.s3.prompt: Nari talk say na 17. Guess where Nari fit make mistake, then write counting method wey fit prevent the same mistake.
z-m-04-02.s.s3.hint.0: First check whether 17 pass or below 16, then think whether dem miss something or count extra.
z-m-04-02.s.s3.hint.1: Think about what kind mark you fit put on things wey you don count so you no count the same sticker twice.
z-m-04-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: The mistake wey I guess fit explain number 17?
z-m-04-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: If I use the method wey I write, e fit prevent both Jihu and Nari mistakes?
z-m-04-02.s.s3.model.0: E seem say dem count the same star two times. If you make small mark on each star wey you don count as you dey count, you no go count any two times or miss any.
z-m-04-02.s.s3.model.1: E seem say dem count one thing extra between middle row and bottom row. If you count each row separately and write am down, then join them later, you fit find the wrong row.
z-m-04-02.s.s3.modelNote.1: Count each row and write am down

z-m-04-04.title: The one wey plenty people choose dey always pass all the rest together?
z-m-04-04.topic: Make counterexample: compare the thing wey people choose pass with all the rest together
z-m-04-04.goal: Make table wey the claim 'the activity wey people choose pass always get more people than all the others put together' no work, then talk the condition wey go make the claim correct.
z-m-04-04.material: 12 friends choose the activity wey dem wan do for picnic. The activities na treasure hunt, skipping rope and ball games. All 12 choose only one thing. Hayun talk, 'The activity wey people choose pass always get more friends than the other two activities put together!' Make we suppose only one activity get the most choices, no tie with another activity.
z-m-04-04.thinking.2: Find the condition wey go make the claim correct
z-m-04-04.prereq.1: Find the biggest thing for a table
z-m-04-04.s.s1.prompt: Hayun claim always correct? Before you make table, choose wetin you think.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.hint.0: Put one small number and write one case.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.hint.1: Put side by side the number for the activity wey people choose pass and the number wey you get wen you add the other two activities.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.o.a: E always correct. The activity wey people choose pass get more than the other activities
z-m-04-04.s.s1.r.a: 'More than each of the other activities' no mean the same thing as 'more than all the rest put together'.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.o.b: E no seem say e always correct. I go test am by putting numbers.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.r.b: You see say the claim talk 'always', so e good to test am. Na way to check with numbers.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.o.c: I no know. We no fit tell because na 12 people.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.r.c: The number of people fixed. Think whether you fit find out by putting in numbers.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.explain: Even one example fit prove the word 'always' wrong. You fit find out by testing with table wey you make yourself. Student wey first talk 'I no know' fit judge after making table too.
z-m-04-04.s.s1.acc.0: At first, you fit no know. You fit find out by making table and testing. E okay if you wan test am.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 tables wey show say Hayun claim no correct. Write number of friends for activity wey get most as a, second as b, and third as c. (a, b, and c na natural numbers wey be 0 or more, and all three together na 12 friends.)
z-m-04-04.s.s2.hint.0: First choose number a of friends for activity wey get most choices.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.hint.1: Count the friends wey choose the other two activities together and compare with a.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.hint.2: Tie no suppose dey. Check say a pass b and c.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.var.a: Number of friends for activity wey get most choices (a)
z-m-04-04.s.s2.var.b: Number of friends for another activity (b)
z-m-04-04.s.s2.var.c: Number of friends for the remaining activity (c)
z-m-04-04.s.s2.ok.c1: Number of friends na natural number wey be 0 or more.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Number of friends must be natural number wey be 0 or more.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.ok.c2: All 12 friends choose one thing each.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.fail.c2: All three numbers must add up to 12 friends.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.ok.c3: a na the activity wey get most choices (no tie dey).
z-m-04-04.s.s2.fail.c3: a must pass both b and c.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.ok.c4: The activity wey get most choices no get more people than all the rest together, so Hayun claim fail.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.fail.c4: For this table, the activity wey get most choices get more people than the rest together, so Hayun claim no fail.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.explain: With 5, 4, 3, the 5 people wey choose am pass get less than the rest, 4 + 3 = 7. With 6, 3, 3, the 6 equal the rest, 3 + 3 = 6, so you no fit talk say 'more'. So Hayun claim no always correct. One table don enough.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.prompt: Choose one table wey you make and write how you go show your friend say Hayun claim wrong.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.hint.0: Choose one table and first write the number for the activity wey get most choices.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.hint.1: Compare that number with the number wey you get wen you count the friends wey choose the other two activities together.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: For the table wey I choose, you use numbers explain why the activity wey get most choices no get more than the other two together?
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You know and write say one table enough to prove the word 'always' wrong?
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.model.0: If na treasure hunt 5, skipping rope 4 and ball games 3, treasure hunt get most, but e less than the 7 for skipping rope and ball games together.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.model.1: If na 6, 3, 3, the 6 people wey choose most equal the 6 wey you get wen you put the other 3 and 3 together, so you no fit talk say e more.
z-m-04-04.s.s2.because.modelNote.1: Use the equal case as counterexample
z-m-04-04.s.s3.prompt: For Hayun claim to always correct, wetin must different? Choose all the correct ones.
z-m-04-04.s.s3.hint.0: Compare with the tables wey you don make, then think wetin must different so Hayun claim no go fail.
z-m-04-04.s.s3.hint.1: Change the number for the activity wey get most choices one by one, then compare am with the total for all the rest.
z-m-04-04.s.s3.o.a: Wen the friends increase from 12 to 15
z-m-04-04.s.s3.r.a: Even if more people dey, you fit make similar tables. How table wey you test with 15 go look?
z-m-04-04.s.s3.o.b: Wen na only two activities dey and number of friends different
z-m-04-04.s.s3.r.b: You look at the fact say wen only two activities dey, you compare the one wey get most choices with the rest (the other activity).
z-m-04-04.s.s3.o.c: Wen one friend fit choose two activities
z-m-04-04.s.s3.r.c: If you count one person two times, only the total number go change, and the comparison problem go remain the same.
z-m-04-04.s.s3.o.d: Wen the activity wey get most choices get 7 or more
z-m-04-04.s.s3.r.d: You work out say if 7 or more out of the 12 choose the same activity, the rest na 5 or less.
z-m-04-04.s.s3.explain: If only two activities dey and the number of friends different, the one wey more people choose get more than the rest (the one other activity). With three activities and 12 friends, if the one wey get most choices get 7 or more, the rest na 5 or less, so the activity wey get most choices get more. Even if you increase the total to 15, tables wey break the rule still dey, like 6, 5, 4.

z-m-04-08.title: Same buttons, but most common one different
z-m-04-08.topic: 'Most' change based on standard: color, shape, type
z-m-04-08.goal: Learn say when you sort same buttons by color, shape, or type combining color and shape, 'most' fit differ; choose standard matching question and make new question.
z-m-04-08.material: Button shop get 12 buttons. Each red, blue, or yellow, and circle or triangle shaped. [Table] Red circle 2 / Red triangle 3 / Blue circle 4 / Blue triangle 0 / Yellow circle 1 / Yellow triangle 2. Total 12. Minjun count by color and by shape too.
z-m-04-08.thinking.0: Sorting same data by different standards and comparing
z-m-04-08.thinking.1: Separating wetin each standard tell from wetin no tell
z-m-04-08.prereq.1: Sorting things by color and shape
z-m-04-08.s.s1.prompt: Na wetin Minjun think. Choose wrong line.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.hint.0: Find and read number inside 'red circle' box in table.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.hint.1: Compare which of six boxes get biggest number.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.line.0: I count by color: red 5, blue 4, yellow 3. Most common color na red.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.line.1: I count by shape: circle 7, triangle 5. Most common shape na circle.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.line.2: So red-circle button na the one wey get the most.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.line.3: Whether you count by color or shape, total na 12.
z-m-04-08.s.s1.explain: Line 3 wrong. Table get only 2 red circles. Putting together the colour wey get most (red) and the shape wey get most (circle) no show the kind of button wey plenty pass. If you count kind where both colour and shape same, blue circle get most with 4. Lines 1 and 2 match table, and line 4 correct too.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.prompt: Choose all the statements wey match wetin the button shop owner wan do with the correct table.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.hint.0: First talk whether the question dey ask about colour, shape, or both.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.hint.1: Find one by one which table show the numbers wey the question need.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.o.a: To decide 'Which box shape we suppose buy more?', you fit look the table wey dem sort by colour
z-m-04-08.s.s2.r.a: The table wey dem count by colour no show number for each shape. Match wetin the question ask with wetin the table tell you.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.o.b: To decide 'Which thread colour we suppose buy more?', you fit look the table wey dem sort by colour
z-m-04-08.s.s2.r.b: The question ask about colour, so you choose the table wey dem count by colour.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.o.c: One table wey dem sort by colour enough for any question
z-m-04-08.s.s2.r.c: You think say one table fit answer every question. Different questions fit need different tables.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.o.d: If you put the colour wey get most together with the shape wey get most, you go get the kind wey get most
z-m-04-08.s.s2.r.d: Check again inside the table boxes whether putting the most for colour and the most for shape together work.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.o.e: To answer 'Which button we suppose restock first?', you need look all six boxes
z-m-04-08.s.s2.r.e: You think say question wey look at colour and shape together need table wey count both colour and shape.
z-m-04-08.s.s2.explain: For question about colour, table wey count by colour fit; for question about shape, table wey count by shape fit; and for question about colour and shape together, table wey look all six boxes fit. One table no fit answer every question.
z-m-04-08.s.s3.prompt: Make another question wey button shop owner fit ask. Also write which table fit the question, the one wey count by colour, by shape, or by colour and shape together, and why.
z-m-04-08.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine wetin button shop owner wan buy.
z-m-04-08.s.s3.hint.1: Try the table wey count by colour, the one wey count by shape, and the six-box table against the question one after another, and see whether answer come out.
z-m-04-08.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Which ... we suppose buy more? ...
z-m-04-08.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You choose the table wey fit the question wey I make?
z-m-04-08.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write why the table wey I choose fit this question pass the other tables?
z-m-04-08.s.s3.model.0: 'Which shape of box we suppose buy more?' For this question, you fit look the table wey dem sort by shape, because e tell you circle 7 and triangle 5.
z-m-04-08.s.s3.model.1: Which kind button we suppose restock first? The table wey count colour and shape together fit, because e tell you blue circle get most with 4.
z-m-04-08.s.s3.modelNote.1: Choose the table wey count colour and shape together

z-m-04-05.title: Survey about favourite colours: which boxes we need?
z-m-04-05.topic: Choose survey questions: make boxes wey everybody fit mark without leaving anybody out
z-m-04-05.goal: Learn the problem wey happen if one survey item no get box, make boxes by yourself so every friend fit mark one box, and talk the limit of the new box wey appear.
z-m-04-05.material: Minho class get 20 students, dem dey do survey on 'one favorite color'. Each person mark only one box. Minho make only three boxes on form: 'red', 'blue', and 'yellow'.
z-m-04-05.thinking.0: Finding wetin missing for survey boxes
z-m-04-05.prereq.0: Marking and counting boxes divided in table (Grade 1 level)
z-m-04-05.prereq.1: Understanding condition say each person choose only one thing
z-m-04-05.s.s1.prompt: If 20 people mark only these three boxes, wetin fit happen?
z-m-04-05.s.s1.hint.0: Think some colors friends fit like.
z-m-04-05.s.s1.hint.1: Check one by one whether each color dey among three boxes.
z-m-04-05.s.s1.o.a: If you count all marks in three boxes, e must be 20
z-m-04-05.s.s1.r.a: Some friends fit get no box to mark. First work out whether every friend fit choose box.
z-m-04-05.s.s1.o.b: Friend wey favorite color green get no cell to mark
z-m-04-05.s.s1.r.b: I match colors friends like to cells in survey table one by one.
z-m-04-05.s.s1.o.c: Only three cells dey, so survey no fit happen at all
z-m-04-05.s.s1.r.c: Few cells no mean survey impossible. Look when cells really become problem.
z-m-04-05.s.s1.o.d: Red go get most marks, so other cells no needed
z-m-04-05.s.s1.r.d: You dey guess box results before time. First check whether every friend fit mark.
z-m-04-05.s.s1.explain: If only three boxes dey, friend wey favorite color no be one of three, like green or purple, get no box. Then total marks fit no reach 20.
z-m-04-05.s.s2.prompt: How you go make boxes so all 20 people fit mark favorite color? Write box names and why you make dem so.
z-m-04-05.s.s2.hint.0: If one of 20 friends like color wey no be red, blue, yellow, think which box dem go mark.
z-m-04-05.s.s2.hint.1: If you add one box, write name wey dem need so everybody fit mark.
z-m-04-05.s.s2.placeholder: Example: Apart from red, blue, yellow boxes, I make ... box because ...
z-m-04-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: With boxes I make, all 20 people fit mark one?
z-m-04-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Any case where one person must mark two boxes?
z-m-04-05.s.s2.model.0: I go make boxes for red, blue, yellow, green and other colors. With 'other colors' box, anybody fit mark no matter wetin color dem like.
z-m-04-05.s.s2.model.1: First ask friends their favorite colors, then make box for every color wey show. Then nobody go lack box to choose.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.prompt: Minho set boxes as 'red, blue, yellow, green, other colors' and survey 20 people. Result: red 4, blue 4, yellow 3, green 3, other colors 6. Jisu talk, 'Other colors get 6, the most, so other colors na most popular color.' How Jisu statement suppose change?
z-m-04-05.s.s3.hint.0: Write some colors wey fit dey inside other-colors box.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.hint.1: Think if all 6 choose same color, and if all 6 choose different colors.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.o.a: Correct. 6 na biggest number, so other colors most popular
z-m-04-05.s.s3.r.a: You compare only numbers in boxes. First think whether 'other colors' na one color.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.o.b: Remove other-colors box and say red and blue most popular
z-m-04-05.s.s3.r.b: Even if you remove box, 6 people wey choose other colors no disappear. You no know which colors those 6 choose.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.o.c: Five cells dey, so result no fit trust
z-m-04-05.s.s3.r.c: Few or many cells no decide whether result trustworthy. Look what information cells give.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.o.d: 'Other colors' mix many colors, so you no fit call am one color
z-m-04-05.s.s3.r.d: You notice many colors gather in one cell. You consider say we no know whether all 6 people in that cell like same color.
z-m-04-05.s.s3.explain: 'Other colors' fit include purple and pink. If all 6 choose different colors, one color fit get 1 person; if all 6 choose same color, one color fit get 6. This table alone no tell us, so ask those 6 which color dem like.

z-m-04-06.title: To say how many more dey
z-m-04-06.topic: Comparing counts for two data sets: pairing and counting separately
z-m-04-06.goal: Compare two ways to find 'how many more'—by pairing and by counted numbers—and make different survey results with same difference.
z-m-04-06.material: Friends in class each choose favorite animal, puppy or cat. Puppy chooser show with ○, cat chooser with △. 8 friends choose puppy and 5 cat. Seohyeon put row of ○ and row of △ side by side, one above other.
z-m-04-06.thinking.1: Making many tables with same difference
z-m-04-06.prereq.0: Comparing number sizes up to 20 and subtracting (Grade 1 level)
z-m-04-06.prereq.1: Comparing by pairing one by one
z-m-04-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose all correct ways to find how many more friends choose puppy than cat.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.hint.0: Put 8 ○ and 5 △ one above other and pair dem one by one.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether answers from methods you choose na same.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.o.a: Pair ○ and △ one by one and count ○ wey no get partner.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.r.a: You pair two rows one by one and look at leftovers for difference. Na pairing comparison.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.o.b: Count all friends wey choose puppy and cat together
z-m-04-06.s.s1.r.b: Total na all friends wey dem survey. Work out whether e tell 'how many more.'
z-m-04-06.s.s1.o.c: Count backward from 8 to 5 and count steps you pass
z-m-04-06.s.s1.r.c: You find difference by counting between numbers. Na different path from pairing, but e find same difference.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.r.d: Bigger number na number of friends wey choose puppy. You never say how many more.
z-m-04-06.s.s1.explain: If you pair dem, 3 ○ remain. Counting back from 8 to 5 also na 3 steps. Both methods give same answer, 3 friends. Total count 13 or bigger number 8 no mean 'how many more.'
z-m-04-06.s.s2.prompt: Another day dem do survey again. Make 3 results where exactly 3 more friends choose puppy than cat, and combined count 15 or less. (At least 1 friend choose cat.)
z-m-04-06.s.s2.hint.0: First choose y, number of friends wey choose cat.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.hint.1: Choose x so paired with your y, 3 ○ remain.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.hint.2: Check both numbers together no pass 15 friends.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.var.x: Number of friends wey choose puppy (x)
z-m-04-06.s.s2.var.y: Number of friends wey choose cat (y)
z-m-04-06.s.s2.ok.c1: Friend counts na natural numbers and at least 1 friend choose cat.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Friend counts must be natural numbers, and at least 1 friend must choose cat.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.ok.c2: Puppy choosers 3 more than cat choosers.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.fail.c2: Exactly 3 more friends must choose puppy than cat.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.ok.c3: Together, both groups total 15 friends or less.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.fail.c3: Friends who choose both animals together must total 15 or less.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.explain: If 1 friend choose cat, puppy count 4; if 5, then 8; if 6, then 9. Each time, pair ○ and △ and 3 ○ remain. Total must be 15 or less, so cat choosers fit reach 6.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.prompt: Even if puppy and cat chooser counts differ across tables, statement 'puppy more by 3' stays true. Explain using pairing ○ and △.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.hint.0: Make table with one more cat chooser, put beside first table, then pair ○ and △.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.hint.1: After pairing, count unmatched ○ in both tables and compare.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You say how many ○ remain unmatched?
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You explain why unmatched ○ count stay same even if more friends choose cat?
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.model.0: If you pair ○ and △ one by one, any table leave 3 unmatched ○. Even if both groups grow by same amount, 3 still remain.
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.modelNote.0: Number left over after pairing stay same
z-m-04-06.s.s2.because.model.1: If one more friend choose cat, one more also choose puppy, so after pairing ○ left still 3.

z-m-04-07.title: Plenty sunny days dey this week. Next week go be the same?
z-m-04-07.topic: Wetin records fit tell and no fit tell: guessing wetin happen next
z-m-04-07.goal: Learn say past records fit show what was 'most' but no fit say for sure wetin happen next; explain how guess change with more records.
z-m-04-07.material: You record weather on classroom calendar for 5 days, Monday to Friday. This week get 3 sunny days, 1 cloudy and 1 rainy. Yeonseo talk, 'Sunny days most this week, so next week sunny days go be most too.'
z-m-04-07.thinking.0: Separating wetin records fit and no fit say
z-m-04-07.prereq.0: Adding numbers up to 5 and reading days count in table (Grade 1 level)
z-m-04-07.prereq.1: Weather words like sunny, cloudy, rainy
z-m-04-07.s.s1.prompt: Right now, wetin you think about Yeonseo statement?
z-m-04-07.s.s1.hint.0: Compare whether 'sunny days most in this week's record' and 'next week's weather' na same statement.
z-m-04-07.s.s1.hint.1: Imagine how things differ if weather records from other weeks dey too.
z-m-04-07.s.s1.o.a: E fit happen, but we no fit know for sure
z-m-04-07.s.s1.r.a: You use past records as clue but no jump to conclusion. Think how more records fit change things.
z-m-04-07.s.s1.o.b: This week's records tell us nothing about next week
z-m-04-07.s.s1.r.b: This week no decide next week, but e no make sense to say no clue at all. Clue and certainty different.
z-m-04-07.s.s1.o.c: E happen this week, so next week e go definitely happen too
z-m-04-07.s.s1.r.c: You carry one week's records straight over to next. Other weeks fit different.
z-m-04-07.s.s1.explain: This week's record na clue say next week sunny days fit plenty. But with only one week's data, you no fit say 'definitely.'
z-m-04-07.s.s1.acc.0: You notice say one week's record no decide next week. Whether e serve as clue fit become clear as we collect more.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.prompt: Yeonseo find last week records too. Last week: 2 sunny, 1 cloudy, 2 rainy. Combine both weeks (10 days): 5 sunny, 2 cloudy, 3 rainy. Choose correct statement.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.hint.0: Count both weeks again by weather and write counts in table.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.hint.1: Write separately wetin records let you say and wetin you no know about next week.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.o.a: Sunny days most, so next week surely sunny days go most too
z-m-04-07.s.s2.r.a: Even with ten days of records, next week never come. More records give more clues, but no certainty.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.o.b: Sunny days most, but next week no known
z-m-04-07.s.s2.r.b: You separate wetin records tell (sunny most) from wetin dem no tell (next week).
z-m-04-07.s.s2.r.c: Compare again the 5 sunny days and 3 rainy days.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.o.d: We collect ten days, so next week go get exactly 3 sunny days
z-m-04-07.s.s2.r.d: You carry past-record ratio straight over to next week. Even with more records, exact next-week day count no decided.
z-m-04-07.s.s2.explain: For ten-day record, you fit say sunny days most, with 5 days. But next week weather never happen, so no decision yet. As records grow, clue say sunny days fit be plenty become a little more believable.
z-m-04-07.s.s3.prompt: From data you get now, write wetin you fit say about next week weather and wetin still uncertain. Also say what more records go make you trust statement more.
z-m-04-07.s.s3.hint.0: Check whether weeks with most sunny days same for this week and last week records.
z-m-04-07.s.s3.hint.1: Think what else you learn if you collect same kind of record for few more weeks.
z-m-04-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: For wetin I say, did I separate 'wetin current data tell' from 'wetin we no know yet'?
z-m-04-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Records I say to collect more of go help guess next week's weather?
z-m-04-07.s.s3.model.0: Sunny days fit be most, but e no certain. If we collect records from more weeks, we fit trust am more.
z-m-04-07.s.s3.model.1: We no know yet. Two weeks no enough, so collect other weeks too and see how often sunny days most.
